data.name: Intro
data.value: Use this when OscarWatch will not start or its window does not appear. It works without OscarWatch running.

data.name: Application.NotFound
data.value: OscarWatch was not found beside the troubleshooter.

data.name: Log.None
data.value: No log files. OscarWatch may have stopped before it could start logging.

data.name: Settings.Missing
data.value: Not found. OscarWatch creates one with default settings when it starts.

data.name: Errors.None
data.value: No errors in the latest log.

data.name: Files.Hint
data.value: Diagnostics include the latest log, your settings with passwords and API keys removed, and system details. Send them to support with a description of the problem.

data.name: Process.Hint
data.value: If OscarWatch is running but no window appears, close it and start it again.

data.name: Hardware.Hint
data.value: If OscarWatch hangs or closes while connecting, turn these off. Ports and other settings are kept, so you can turn them back on in Settings.

data.name: Action.DisableHardware
data.value: Turn off radio, rotator and GPS

data.name: Reset.Hint
data.value: Last resort. Moves settings.json and its backups into a dated folder, so OscarWatch starts with default settings. Nothing is deleted.

data.name: Confirm.CloseOscarWatch
data.value: Close OscarWatch now? Changes it has not saved may be lost.

data.name: Confirm.CloseFirst
data.value: OscarWatch is running. It has to be closed first, or it could undo this change when it exits. Close OscarWatch and continue?

data.name: Confirm.DisableHardware
Confirm.PutSettingsAside
data.value: Move settings.json and its backups into {0}? OscarWatch will start with default settings.

data.name: Result.StillRunning
data.value: OscarWatch is still running, so nothing was changed.

data.name: Result.HardwareDisabled
data.value: Radio, rotator and GPS are now off. Start OscarWatch to check that it opens.

data.name: Result.HardwareAlreadyOff
data.value: Radio, rotator and GPS are already off.

data.name: Result.SettingsMissing
data.value: There is no settings.json to change.

data.name: Result.SettingsUnreadable
data.value: settings.json cannot be read, so it was not changed.

data.name: Result.NothingToMove
data.value: There are no settings files to move.

data.name: Result.FolderOpenFailed
data.value: The folder could not be opened: {0}

data.name: Echo.Hint
data.value: If FT4 transmits off frequency after a bad echo, clear the saved uplink trims. OscarWatch can learn them again from your next echoes.

data.name: Confirm.ClearEchoCalibrations
data.value: Clear all {0} saved FT4 echo calibrations? Every satellite and transponder goes back to no uplink trim.

data.name: Result.EchoCleared
data.value: FT4 echo calibrations cleared. OscarWatch can learn them again from your next echoes.

data.name: Result.EchoNoneSaved
data.value: There are no FT4 echo calibrations to clear.

data.name: Gs232.Hint
data.value: Tests a Yaesu GS-232 compatible rotator controller directly and logs every byte sent and received, including replies OscarWatch normally ignores. OscarWatch has to be closed so the COM port is free. When you report a rotator problem, save this log and attach it.

data.name: Gs232.SettingsUnavailable
data.value: Not available. settings.json is missing or cannot be read, so the rotator port is not known.

data.name: Gs232.NotGs232
data.value: Not available. The rotator in Settings is not a Yaesu GS-232 on a COM port.

data.name: Gs232.NoPort
data.value: Not available. No COM port is set for the rotator in Settings.

data.name: Gs232.Ready
data.value: Ready. Uses the rotator settings saved in OscarWatch.

data.name: Gs232.MoveHint
data.value: Move 5 degrees turns the antenna 5° in azimuth after a confirm, and keeps the elevation. It is available once Read position has returned the azimuth (and the elevation, unless the controller is azimuth only).

data.name: Gs232.LogEmpty
data.value: Nothing sent yet. Each button opens the COM port, logs every byte, and closes it again.

data.name: Confirm.Gs232Move
data.value: Send {0} to the rotator on {1}? The antenna will turn from azimuth {2}° to {3}°. Check nothing is in the way.

data.name: Result.Gs232NoPosition
data.value: The controller did not report a position. The session log shows what came back.

data.name: Result.Gs232Stopped
data.value: Stop sent. The session log shows any reply.

data.name: Result.Gs232LogCopied
data.value: Session log copied to the clipboard.
